quote: Most importantly, I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible.
context: Essay 'The Education of a Libertarian', Cato Unbound.
source_type: primary (his own essay)

quote: Since 1920, the vast increase in welfare beneficiaries and the extension of the franchise to women — two constituencies that are notoriously tough for libertarians — have rendered the notion of “capitalist democracy” into an oxymoron.
context: Same essay. In a follow-up, reproduced in an editor's note on the same Cato page, Thiel wrote: 'It would be absurd to suggest that women’s votes will be taken away or that this would solve the political problems that vex us. While I don’t think any class of people should be disenfranchised, I have little hope that voting will make things better.' Always show both.
source_type: primary (his own essay)

quote: And the NHS makes people sick.
context: Oxford Union inaugural bicentenary address, Monday 16 January 2023 (The Oxford Student, 18 Jan 2023, dates it 'Monday night'). Answering a questioner who noted that Palantir was pursuing a major NHS data contract and asked how he would fix the NHS, Thiel called the NHS 'a very iatrogenic institution', listed 'the highways create traffic jams and welfare creates poverty and the schools make people dumb', then said this line, and added 'the first step is you have to get out of the Stockholm syndrome that uh that that it's that it's anywhere close to working', suggesting 'market mechanisms' and less regulation. Words from the Oxford Union's own upload, at about 64:20-65:30, transcribed from YouTube's auto-captions. Louis Mosley later told MPs Thiel 'was speaking in an entirely personal capacity'. Palantir has led the NHS England Federated Data Platform since Nov 2023.
source_type: primary (Oxford Union video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: probably reference Greta and the the sort of autistic children's crusade.
context: Same Oxford Union address, at about 23:10, on climate change as the 'mass market version of the sort of catastrophic existential risk'. Corrected from the earlier secondary wording ('Greta and the autistic children's crusade', Cherwell), which dropped 'the sort of'. Transcribed from YouTube's auto-captions of the Oxford Union upload.
source_type: primary (Oxford Union video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: I backed Trump for the same reason that if I was in the UK, I would have been a pro-Brexit person.
context: Same Oxford Union address, Q&A, about 47:20, asked why he backed Trump in 2016. He went on to say there was 'a worry that both Trump and Brexit actually delayed that much needed discussion more than they accelerated it.'
source_type: primary (Oxford Union video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: The technology tilts It tilts towards surveillance.
context: Same Oxford Union address, Q&A, about 33:00, answering a question about AI. Just before, he said the most problematic version of AI 'is something like what you see in in communist China where it's it's it's fairly low-tech, but it is just this pervasive surveillance', and that the problem 'is China far more than in the West'.
source_type: primary (Oxford Union video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: Douthat: "You would prefer the human race to endure, right?" ... "You're hesitating." ... "This is a long hesitation." Thiel, when Douthat asked again whether the human race should survive: "Yes."
context: New York Times 'Interesting Times' podcast with Ross Douthat, discussing AI and transhumanism, about 38:15-38:40 of the episode as uploaded by the show's own YouTube channel. Do not quote this as him saying no: after the pause he said yes, and added that he would also like us 'to radically solve these problems'. The NYT's edited transcript (https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/26/opinion/peter-thiel-antichrist-ross-douthat.html) is paywalled; Complex's report matches the same exchange.
source_type: primary (Interesting Times / New York Times video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: I obviously don't think that that's what I'm doing.
context: Same episode, about 56:31. Douthat put it to him that he is invested in Palantir, military technology and 'technologies of surveillance', and asked whether an Antichrist who used fear of technology to impose order would be using the tools Thiel was building. Thiel opened with 'there are all these different scenario' before this answer; Douthat replied that he did not think so either.
source_type: primary (Interesting Times / New York Times video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: In the 21st century, the Antichrist is a Luddite who wants to stop all science. It’s someone like Greta or Eliezer,
context: Opening lecture (15 Sept 2025) of a private, off-the-record four-part series on the Antichrist at the Commonwealth Club, San Francisco, per recordings reviewed by The Washington Post (https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2025/10/10/peter-thiel-antichrist-lectures-leaked/, paywalled beyond its first paragraph). Refers to Greta Thunberg and Eliezer Yudkowsky. Wording as quoted in AFP's report of the Post story.
source_type: secondary (AFP report of recordings reviewed by The Washington Post)

quote: It’s become quite difficult to hide one’s money,
context: Same opening lecture, per AFP's report of the Post story: Thiel described an 'incredible machinery of tax treaties, financial surveillance, and sanctions architecture' that gives wealthy people only an 'illusion of power and autonomy', and treated financial regulation as a sign a world government could emerge.
source_type: secondary (AFP report of recordings reviewed by The Washington Post)

quote: legionnaires of the Antichrist
context: The Washington Post's report of the same lecture series says Thiel described Greta Thunberg and critics of technology or AI in these terms. The phrase is the Post's quotation from the recordings; the exact lecture and date are not visible outside the paywall, so the date given is the Post's publication date.
source_type: secondary (The Washington Post, from leaked recordings)

quote: Our software is used to target terrorists and to keep soldiers safe. If we are going to ask someone to put themselves in harm’s way, we believe that we have a duty to give them what they need to do their job. We have chosen sides, and we know that our partners value our commitment.
context: Karp's letter accompanying Palantir's direct listing (filed with its SEC registration), on the company's mission and customers. He continues: 'We stand by them when it is convenient, and when it is not.'
source_type: primary (his own letter, published by Palantir)

quote: The construction of software platforms that enable more effective surveillance by the state of its adversaries or that assist soldiers in executing attacks raises countless issues, involving the points of tension and tradeoffs between our collective security and individual privacy, the power of machines, and the types of lives we both want to and should lead.
context: Same direct-listing letter, section III, which opens: "Our work and the use of our software present difficult questions."
source_type: primary (his own letter, published by Palantir)

quote: We’re the only company our size that doesn’t buy your data or sell your data. We don’t transfer it to any other entity. That data belongs to the government of the UK.
context: Interview with Victoria Derbyshire on BBC One's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, while NHS England's Federated Data Platform procurement was still open (award followed in Nov 2023). Asked about polling that 48% would likely opt out if a private company ran the FDP, he said other companies 'will take that data and transfer to somebody else' but 'Palantir doesn’t do that.'
source_type: secondary (Digital Health report of the BBC interview)

quote: But by the UK government, not by me. I don’t have the ability to do that,
context: Same BBC interview. Under questioning he acknowledged that once health data was brought together in the FDP it could potentially be sold in future if a government chose to; this was his qualification. He also defended giving software away initially: 'By the way what’s wrong with that?'
source_type: secondary (Digital Health report of the BBC interview)

quote: You know, we are doing in United Kingdom and many other places, Palantir is here to disrupt and make the institutions we partner with the very best in the world and when it's necessary to scare enemies and, on occasion, kill them. And we hope you're in favor of that.
context: Closing remarks to investors on Palantir's Q4 2024 earnings call. Earlier on the same call, chief revenue officer Ryan Taylor said international revenue growth was 'driven in large part by the U.K., including our work with the NHS to roll out the federated data platform'. Palantir's own webcast upload (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MW0zvoEMdRA) has no captions; wording from The Motley Fool's transcript.
source_type: secondary (published transcript of the earnings call)

quote: This partnership reflects our deep commitment to the UK. It will see up to £750m invested in the most advanced AI-enabled defence technology, honed on the battlefield in Ukraine and used extensively by the US and NATO. It will reinforce the UK’s position as a major military force protecting the West from our adversaries. And it will underline the UK’s status as our largest presence outside of the US.
context: Quoted in the Ministry of Defence press release announcing the UK-Palantir strategic partnership (up to £1.5bn of Palantir investment; London as its European defence HQ; opportunities 'worth up to £750 million over the next five years'), signed by Defence Secretary John Healey. The release says the work supports the 'kill chain' and the Digital Targeting Web.
source_type: official (UK government press release quoting him)

quote: The ability of free and democratic societies to prevail requires something more than moral appeal. It requires hard power, and hard power in this century will be built on software.
context: Point 4 of 'The Technological Republic, in brief', a 22-point summary of the 2025 book by Karp and Nicholas W. Zamiska posted on Palantir's corporate X account ('Because we get asked a lot.'). The Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee quoted this point in its June 2026 report, contrasting it with Louis Mosley's evidence that Palantir 'is not... political'. The public X embed shows only the start of the long post; the full text was checked against Engadget's reproduction (https://www.engadget.com/big-tech/palantir-posted-a-manifesto-that-reads-like-the-ramblings-of-a-comic-book-villain-181947361.html).
source_type: primary (Palantir post of excerpts from his co-written book)

quote: We must resist the shallow temptation of a vacant and hollow pluralism. We, in America and more broadly the West, have for the past half century resisted defining national cultures in the name of inclusivity. But inclusion into what?
context: Point 22 of the same post (book co-written with Nicholas W. Zamiska). Times Radio put this point to Louis Mosley in Aug 2026; he said he did not think the points were 'incompatible' with Palantir's NHS role.
source_type: primary (Palantir post of excerpts from his co-written book)

quote: Some cultures have produced vital advances; others remain dysfunctional and regressive.
context: Point 21 of the same post (book co-written with Nicholas W. Zamiska).
source_type: primary (Palantir post of excerpts from his co-written book)

quote: Sometimes we make decisions like that are against our economic interest, like we're supporting lots of institutions in Europe, the growth sucks. I mean, Clandestine institutions. But without our products, they would have rampant terrorism and their problems, their migration problems and the results would be 10 times worse.
context: Palantir Q2 2026 earnings call, on why Palantir stays aligned with its partners. He went on: 'It's not actually in our economic interest anymore to do this, but we still do it. And it's because we actually are believers for better or worse.' Palantir's own webcast upload has no captions; wording from The Motley Fool's transcript (diginomica's rendering differs slightly).
source_type: secondary (published transcript of the earnings call)

quote: I’m more convinced than ever that the UK is uniquely placed to pioneer the next generation of medical discoveries and treatments
context: Email to NHS England chair David Prior after a dinner Mosley hosted on 2 July 2019, the eve of NHSX's launch, at which they discussed future uses of NHS data. From emails released to the Bureau of Investigative Journalism under FOI. Mosley was then described as Palantir's UK boss. Prior replied inviting help to 'structure and curate our data'.
source_type: secondary (Digital Health report of FOI emails)

quote: “Buying our way in…!”
context: Subject line of an internal email (Sept 2021), first reported by Bloomberg on 30 Sept 2022 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-09-30/palantir-had-plan-to-crack-uk-health-system-buying-our-way-in), suggesting 'hoovering up' existing NHS suppliers could 'take a lot of ground and take down a lot of political resistance'. A Palantir spokesperson told Bloomberg the language was 'regrettable' and 'not an accurate characterisation of our relationship with the NHS'. In Aug 2026 Mosley called it 'a thought experiment about a potential strategy which we never pursued' and said he meant 'small P political resistance', i.e. competition. Quoted here as reported by Liberty Investigates; Bloomberg's text is paywalled.
source_type: secondary (Liberty Investigates, citing documents seen by Bloomberg)

quote: HMG should invest in a "Common Operating System" ("System") solution that would sit on top of, and be able to integrate with, the multitude of source systems across the local and central government, healthcare and other bodies of national strategic importance.
context: Witness statement to the UK Covid-19 Inquiry (Module 5), signed as 'Executive Vice President of Palantir Technologies UK, Ltd.' In its conclusions it recommends the system's scope 'be as broad as possible, including other government departments like the Department of Work and Pensions (DWP) or Local Authorities (LAs)', and says government should deploy it 'immediately'.
source_type: primary (his witness statement)

quote: we use AI to defend the West against its enemies and make western governments more efficient in the US we are seeing government reforms that will change the lives of everyone in that country for the better there is no reason we cannot do the same here in Britain and elsewhere across [Applause] Europe
context: Speech to the Alliance for Responsible Citizenship (ARC) conference in London, as uploaded by ARC (date is the upload date). The speech argued a 'regime we might call globalism' depended on 'narrative control and censorship', said those who challenged the official narrative on 'the origins of the covid pandemic or mass migration have felt the weight of this whole of society effort', and warned that AI 'could in the wrong hands become the most powerful tool of censorship tyranny and dehumanization'. Captions are unpunctuated.
source_type: primary (conference video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: You could see in his eyes that he gets it
context: The House magazine interview, billed as his first sit-down interview; on meeting Keir Starmer at Palantir's Washington office in Feb 2025. He added: 'The ambition is there – the will is there.'
source_type: secondary (magazine interview)

quote: We would welcome competitors of any country, apart from Russia and China.
context: Same interview, asked whether he would welcome British competitors. He described Palantir as a "layer of a stack" that other UK software vendors can build on.
source_type: secondary (magazine interview)

quote: It’s a constant reminder of: you’re building a very, very powerful tool, and in the wrong hands, very powerful tools can be extremely dangerous. But in the right hands, they can be used to do extraordinarily good things.
context: Same interview, on whether he worries about the company's name, taken from Tolkien's 'seeing stones'.
source_type: secondary (magazine interview)

quote: The decision was made to charge £1 because of some procurement process whereby we needed to be on a payment system in order for the contract to be stood up, but it was really a token.
context: Oral evidence to the Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee (Q107), where he was listed as 'Executive Vice-President, Palantir' and said he leads 'our business here in the UK and across Europe'. On the 2020 Covid data store: 'We offered, because it was a national emergency, to provide our support free.' He compared try-before-you-buy to a discounted newspaper subscription; the chair said it can discriminate against smaller firms.
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: The critical thing to bear in mind about the way our software works and the way it is deployed in the NHS is that the data controllers, the organisations that have legal responsibility, which in the NHS are typically trusts, maintain control over their data.
context: Same session (Q109), asked whether any NHS data is processed outside the UK or could be seized by a foreign government. The chair said he had 'not quite answered the question'. PA's widely syndicated version (e.g. LBC) words it slightly differently; this is the official transcript.
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: In the NHS’s case, all the data is stored in the public cloud. It is stored in the London region of AWS, which is Amazon Web Services. In that sense, it is all resident in the UK and it is not exported elsewhere.
context: Same session (Q110). He added that UK residency requirements are 'currently the case in every instance of our deployment across the NHS' (Q111) and that 'the NHS’s instance of the software is not accessible to anyone outside the UK' (Q114), while software is maintained by teams in the UK, US and Singapore.
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: We do not derive any economic benefit from the data. The data belongs to the customer.
context: Same session (Q116), on whether Palantir has any NHS revenue beyond licence and support. Quoted by the committee in its June 2026 report alongside Medconfidential's warning that Palantir would try to "burrow so deep into the NHS that they cannot be migrated away from".
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: Technically, I think it is extremely low.
context: Same session (Q120), asked 'what is the risk that the NHS becomes locked into your software?'. Pressed by the chair (Q122) on what a customer can take away, he said 'They own the data and the logic—the content of it' but 'they would need to have some substitute for the connections'.
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: However, if our services are very useful and they enable the Government to deliver very important outcomes, arguably that creates a form of dependency.
context: Same session (Q138), asked about government dependency on Palantir. He first said 'there is no technical lock-in, so the dependency is not technical', and said the way to manage it is 'commercially'.
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: If I may be frank, I think that the BMA has chosen ideology over patient interest.
context: Same session (Q127), responding to the BMA's June 2025 motion calling Palantir 'an unacceptable choice of partner' for the FDP. He also said: 'I think the accusation that we lack transparency or that this is secretive is wrong.' Widely reported (Guardian, PA/LBC, Irish News); one entry here.
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: He was speaking in an entirely personal capacity. He was not speaking for Palantir, and he certainly was not speaking for me.
context: Same session (Q139), on Peter Thiel's Oxford Union remarks about the NHS. He said there would be 'general disagreement across the company' with Thiel's NHS views, and that Karp had said 'effectively, the diametric opposite' (that is Mosley's account of Karp, not a Karp quote).
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: We are here to support democratically elected Governments in delivering the mandate that they have been elected to deliver, and to do so subject to the rule of law.
context: Same session (Q139). Preceded by: 'We do not—unlike some tech companies, I am afraid—pick and choose which Government policies we will support and which ones we will not.' The committee's June 2026 report set this and his statement that Palantir 'is not... political' against the company's 22-point manifesto.
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: We work in Israel; we are proud of the work we do there.
context: Same session (Q146), asked what protections would stop UK programmes being complicit in war crimes. He said Palantir has supported Israel since 7 October and before, could not give operational details, and that 'the systems to which you might be alluding, like Lavender, are not ones in which we are involved'. Asked (Q144-145) whether its AI could help target individuals with particular characteristics, he said Palantir provides 'an enormous amount of control and governance'; MP Kit Malthouse replied: 'That sounds like a yes.'
source_type: primary (Hansard-style committee transcript)

quote: So we we we exist to support whichever is the government of the day to deliver on the policies and plans they've been elected to deliver on.
context: Interview uploaded by 'The Tech Report' YouTube channel, asked whether voters should worry about Palantir's founder's politics. He also said 'we only work with western aligned countries' and that what the NHS discloses about Palantir's work is 'in the end the decision of the NHS'.
source_type: primary (interview video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: We’re only just getting started. We’ll look back in five years’ time and we’ll think those were small deals.
context: In a podcast appearance on the day the UK-Palantir defence partnership was announced, per Liberty Investigates (the podcast is not named there).
source_type: secondary (Liberty Investigates report of a podcast)

quote: a programme that needs to be decided at the ballot box, not in the company boardroom
context: Times Radio, early Oct 2025, saying Palantir would not bid for the government's planned digital ID: 'We’re seeing a wide divergence of views and a lot of controversy around it ... So, it isn’t one for us.' He also questioned its 'technical necessity', saying existing identifiers could be linked 'in the backend with relatively little effort'. As reported by Liberty Investigates.
source_type: secondary (Liberty Investigates report of a Times Radio interview)

quote: So, I think the the question of how you keep humans in the loop is going to be a policy question. Technologically, unfortunately, I think we're moving in a direction where much of the process can be automated.
context: Bloomberg Tech Europe interview on AI in defence; he said 'the moment of American unipolarity is over' and called Ukraine 'the R&D lab for AI in a military context'. The same interview was uploaded twice more by Bloomberg (QUy_6mDaEPQ, R9vKXEWxXpw); one entry here.
source_type: primary (Bloomberg video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: So, where uh a government has has a democratic mandate, uh there is an effect public consent for a policy, we would see it as our duty to help deliver that.
context: Washington Post Live interview with David Ignatius, on Palantir's ICE work, which he said began 'under President Obama'. Asked about privacy, he said Palantir's founders rejected a one-to-one trade-off between security and civil liberties: 'With the right technology, you could have more of both.'
source_type: primary (Washington Post Live video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: Well, we've had a policy since the very inception of Palanteer that we we exist to help the West win.
context: Sky News interview from Davos ('Palanteer' is the auto-caption spelling of Palantir). On the NHS: 'They simply use our software to process it which means Palanteer does not have access to that information. We don't monetize that information.' He said Green leader Zack Polanski was 'putting ideology ideology over over patients'.
source_type: primary (Sky News video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: Having a review clause in a contract is good and normal practice. However, what some ideologically motivated campaigners are suggesting should happen would harm patient care and prevent some of the biggest challenges facing the NHS from being tackled,
context: Told The Times, as ministers explored using the FDP contract's break clause; quoted by the Guardian (which calls him 'executive vice-chair').
source_type: secondary (Guardian report of a Times interview)

quote: in the same way that Microsoft Excel or Microsoft Word or email is used in the NHS, and again, that is NHS data. Microsoft doesn't have access to it, nor do we to NHS data.
context: BBC Politics Live, debating Faiza Shaheen after Green leader Zack Polanski called for the FDP contract to end. In the same answer he said the Israeli targeting systems 'are called Lavender and Gospel. We have nothing to do with them.' In May 2026 he described Palantir's FDP access as 'a specific technical permission inside one staging environment' (see that entry); the Commons committee set the two statements side by side.
source_type: primary (BBC video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: they're finding it harder and harder therefore to to make the case because uh the truth is the software works. And um unlike many experiences with IT that the NHS has had, it is delivering real tangible benefits.
context: Centre for Policy Studies conference panel (CapX upload, 29 Apr 2026), on the Green Party's campaign; he said Zack Polanski had 'turned up at our office in London uh with a mob uh back in January' to pin a 'dismissal letter' to the door. The Guardian (27 Apr 2026) printed a tidied version of the same remark.
source_type: primary (conference video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: he's putting his ideology over patient lives, patient safety.
context: Full interview uploaded by the 'etn.' YouTube channel, on Zack Polanski. Similar to his Jan 2026 Sky News remark and the 'chosen ideology over patient safety' line reported by the Guardian in July 2026.
source_type: primary (interview video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: a specific technical permission inside one staging environment
context: His response, in a post on X, to a May 2026 Financial Times report that Palantir had been given 'unlimited access' to identifiable patient data while working on part of the FDP; he said the permission was held by 'fewer than five Palantir employees who are UK-based, vetted and approved by NHS engineering leadership'. As quoted in the Commons committee's report, which contrasts it with his April statement comparing Palantir to Microsoft. The committee asked the government to confirm 'the exact nature of Palantir’s access'.
source_type: secondary (Commons committee report quoting his X post)

quote: What Londoners value is not being mugged, not being raped by a serving police officer and that’s really what the focus here should be … If we are going to politicise procurement in that way then we are going to compromise public safety
context: Times Radio, after the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime blocked the Met's proposed £50m Palantir contract; quoted by the Guardian. He also questioned why Sadiq Khan took exception 'with our values and not with other tech companies'. Labour MP Stella Creasy said he 'should be ashamed of himself'.
source_type: secondary (Guardian report of a Times Radio interview)

quote: putting politics over public safety
context: Accusation against the Mayor of London as Palantir sent MOPAC a pre-action letter (first reported by The Times), as summarised by Local Government Lawyer around 11 June 2026.
source_type: secondary (Local Government Lawyer, citing The Times)

quote: The British state has used us in two departments that have since stopped using us and had no issues with transferring the data, the logic, the intellectual property that they developed in our software out of our software and into other vendors. So this notion that we are part of a vendor lock-in is false
context: BBC Radio 4 Today programme, early June 2026, after the Commons committee called Palantir 'an unacceptable point of weakness'; quoted by the Guardian on 8 June 2026 ('last week').
source_type: secondary (Guardian report of a radio interview)

quote: I don't think it's appropriate for unelected self-appointed tech bosses to decide what is democratic or what is lawful.
context: Channel 4 News full interview, on Palantir's ICE contract after deaths in Minneapolis. He said ICE work began under Obama, that there was 'a very live debate internally', and that withdrawing would be 'countermanding a decision that was taken at the ballot box'. Asked about the Feb 2026 Minab school strike in Iran, he first said 'We were not involved' and later 'I don't know, frankly, whether we were or were not involved', citing a classified US investigation.
source_type: primary (Channel 4 News video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: Well, we have no more access to it than say Microsoft has access to the contents of a word document or an Excel spreadsheet that you might be using at home.
context: Same Channel 4 News interview, on an FT report about engineers' access to patient data. On the FDP break clause: 'that is not for me to decide again that will be for the elected politicians of this country to decide'.
source_type: primary (Channel 4 News video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: procurement should be done on the basis of quality, performance, value for money, not on highly subjective measures like values.
context: Same interview, on the Mayor's block of the Met contract. He said Palantir was considering legal proceedings and was 'not yet suing'.
source_type: primary (Channel 4 News video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: our software is used to generate a list of targets.
context: Same interview, on the US military's Maven system. He stressed: 'It's always a human' who decides, and that the software keeps an auditable record. He also said Palantir software was used in Israel 'to identify, track, and locate missing hostages' and that neither of the two publicly reported Gaza targeting systems uses it.
source_type: primary (Channel 4 News video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: Well, firstly, this is not a decision that we've taken lightly and it's one that we take frankly quite reluctantly.
context: Sky News, on Palantir taking MOPAC to court over the blocked Met contract; he said the mayor's office had been 'uncooperative and opaque'. On the NHS: 'we don't have access to the data. The data remains entirely under the control and ownership of the NHS.' Also uploaded by the Ridge & Frost channel (_C9ocuj4GlM); one entry here.
source_type: primary (Sky News video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: And the government should be thinking very hard about how to secure that sovereign capability.
context: Same Sky News interview: he called the US government's forced withdrawal of an Anthropic model 'a canary in the coal mine' and said dependence on such technology 'arguably a critical supply chain risk', but that companies like Palantir need not be 'domestic champions'. Asked if a US president could order Palantir to stop serving foreign governments: 'That would be a breach of contracts, it would be a breach of the law.' He said the NHS and MoD 'control and own their versions of Palantir software'.
source_type: primary (Sky News video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: We we're ultimately a US company. We're headquartered in America.
context: Times Radio, on the Defence Investment Plan and sovereignty: 'can the British Ministry of Defense be absolutely certain that it has full operational control over its use of our software and that's where we have been through an exhaustive process to ensure that that's the case.' He also said 2026 may be seen as the year 'autonomous warfare became real' and that who decides should 'not' be 'left to technology companies like mine'.
source_type: primary (Times Radio video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: we do draw some very strict red lines and have done from the very inception of the company
context: Interview with Harry Cole ('Harry Cole Saves The West'), asked where Palantir's line is, having declined digital ID. He described the Met professional-standards work and said the blocked contract would have extended it to 'serious organized crime, domestic abuse, every category of of crime'.
source_type: primary (interview video; quoted from YouTube auto-captions)

quote: I hope that competitors will emerge. Uh I think that will be good for everyone but at the moment there aren't any. We we are in a class of our own.
context: The Spectator's 'Quite right!' interview, as Andy Burnham took office. On reports Burnham would scrap the FDP contract: 'I have no grounds to believe they're true. And obviously I think it'd be a terrible mistake.' The video's headline 'ditching Palantir would put politics ahead of patient care' is the interviewer's phrasing, to which Mosley answered 'Yes.' A shorter cut was uploaded on 18 July (heEgv-tKWa4).

quote: If the NHS were to choose to try and monetize that with drug companies for research purposes, that's a decision for the government, for the NHS, not for us. But it's absolutely something we could enable.
